name: Grammarly
tagline: Writing assistant that checks grammar, spelling, tone and plagiarism and offers AI writing help; run by Superhuman Platform Inc.

evidence.quote: This Privacy Policy describes how Superhuman Platform Inc. (formerly Grammarly) and our subsidiaries
Superhuman Platform Inc. , formerly known as Grammarly, Inc.

vendor_entity.note: Formerly Grammarly, Inc. The consumer terms, Customer Business Agreement and DPA name the same entity. Grammarly Inc. is now listed as a subsidiary.

evidence.quote: Superhuman Platform Inc., 2261 Market Street, STE 85232, San Francisco, CA 94114
Grammarly acquires Coda (now Superhuman Docs) and Superhuman Mail, launching Superhuman as the unified brand.

parent_company.note: No parent or owner is named on the privacy policy, terms, CBA, DPA, sub-processor page, trust page, Grammarly about page or Superhuman about page. The Superhuman about page says Grammarly acquired Coda and Superhuman Mail in 2025 and took the Superhuman name, so the former Grammarly company is the top entity; Grammarly Inc., Coda Project LLC, Superhuman Labs LLC and GPTZero are its subsidiaries. Investor lists on third-party sites were not used.

evidence.quote: This Privacy Policy describes how Superhuman Platform Inc. (formerly Grammarly) and our subsidiaries

parent_country.note: No separate parent named (see parent_company). The contracting company itself is in the US.

evidence.quote: We’ve appointed VeraSafe as our representative in the EEA and UK for data protection matters.
Superhuman Platform Inc. has appointed Bird & Bird DPO Services SRL as its Data Protection Officer (DPO).

dpo_contact.note: The DPO is an outsourced service firm; no individual is named.

evidence.quote: Grammarly hosts data in Amazon Web Services data centers in the US East region
provided by Amazon Web Services (AWS) and/or Google Cloud Platform (GCP), located in the United States

hosting_regions.note: Grammarly product: AWS US East (security page). The DPA security exhibit says the services are hosted in the United States.

local_first.note: Pages read do not say whether content can be kept only on the device. No local-only mode is described.

eu_residency.note: Only US hosting is stated (security page, DPA security exhibit). No EU data-residency option was found. DPA section 9(a) says data may be processed in the United States and other locations.

evidence.quote: Grammarly is hosted on Amazon Web Services (AWS).
The Services are hosted on enterprise-grade cloud infrastructure provided by Amazon Web Services (AWS) and/or Google Cloud Platform (GCP)

cloud_providers.note: Grammarly itself is hosted on AWS (DPA product section, security page). GCP is named for the Superhuman services as a whole; the 2026-11-16 DPA no longer says which product uses it (the earlier version named Superhuman Mail). Google is also listed as an infrastructure sub-processor. Other infrastructure sub-processors (CoreWeave, Turbopuffer, Databricks) are listed without saying which product they host.

transfer_mechanism.note: The DPF participant list on dataprivacyframework.gov was read only as its page shell (the list is a downloadable spreadsheet). DPF status is the vendor's statement, not checked against the list.

retention_stated.note: No fixed periods in days or years for Grammarly content; saved documents are kept until the user deletes them or the account. For Docs (not Grammarly) the DPA gives 7 days in primary storage plus 35 days in backups after deletion.

evidence.quote: will, at the written request of Customer, make available for return to Customer and/or securely destroy all Customer Personal Data

deletion_on_exit.note: No time frame is stated after termination. Backups are deleted 'in accordance with its deletion practices' (DPA section 11).

evidence.quote: Customer will have the ability within its account settings to export and/or delete its Customer Data

trains_on_content.footnote: Free, Premium and single-user Pro accounts, and multi-user teams bought on the website: content is used for training by default and can be turned off (opt-out).

evidence.quote: Customer data and text are never sold or used to train models.
For all Grammarly for Education, Grammarly Business, Pro, and Grammarly Enterprise accounts purchased through our Sales team, Product Improvement and Training is automatically off
will not use Customer Data to train any generative artificial intelligence models without Customer’s prior written consent.
Product Improvement and Training is on for individual users by default.

trains_on_content.note: Institutional answer (Education and accounts bought through Sales). The help article says the control covers training and validating AI and ML models, so this is model training, not only service improvement. Non-content writing statistics may still be used. The privacy policy says AI service providers are restricted from training on user content.

ai_zero_retention.note: No zero-retention or no-logging statement for model providers in the DPA, trust, security, privacy, responsible-AI or training-control pages. source blocked: https://help.superhuman.com/hc/en-us/articles/47716615380109-Superhuman-Go-Data-Privacy-FAQ (a Superhuman Go page, not Grammarly).

evidence.quote: Account admins can control whether or not to turn on certain AI features

ai_admin_off.note: Admins control 'certain' AI features. The responsible AI page adds that admins can restrict domains and apps.

ai_act_statement.note: No EU AI Act position or transparency statement on the AI, responsible-AI, trust or security pages. A Grammarly business explainer page describes the AI Act in general terms but gives no Grammarly position. ISO/IEC 42001 is claimed (see certifications).
